name: Joomla
description: Joomla is a free, open-source content management system built entirely by volunteers, used to build websites and online applications with multilingual and permission-based content control.
best_for: Organizations that need multilingual websites, granular user permissions, and full design customization without licensing costs.

tiers.name: Joomla Core
tiers.notes: GPL-licensed, free to download, install, and modify indefinitely; self-hosting costs (server, PHP/MySQL) are the buyer's own responsibility.

cons: Joomla core has no built-in e-commerce or advanced functionality -- sites depend on third-party extensions of uneven quality, and Joomla's own docs maintain a Vulnerable Extensions List with an explicit warning that it does not guarantee the quality or effectiveness of listed extensions' updates.

Joomla 6 requires PHP 8.3 or newer and MySQL 8.0.13+/MariaDB 10.4.0+, and Joomla 4 already reached end of life in October 2025 -- site owners must self-manage version upgrades and hosting-stack compatibility with no vendor support cushion.

Joomla's own community magazine has published self-critical coverage of the project's declining market share and internal governance conflicts; independent tracking puts Joomla around 1-2% of all websites versus WordPress's 60%+, meaning a much smaller extension and developer ecosystem.
features: Built-in multi-language support for content and interface
Multi-user permission levels and access control groups
Fully extensible developer framework for custom builds
Completely free and open source with no vendor lock-in
